content.content:
\begin{description}
\item[Affected section] \secref{FortressBuiltin}: the comment of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive} in the \apiN\ \TYP{FortressBuiltin}, which this
specification typesets from the \apiN's source file.
\item[Change] The comment says that the argument of \VAR{builtinPrimitive}
names either a glue class, a subclass of
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeApp}, which only the
interpreter runs, or a helper, a public static method of a Java class of the
package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, which both the interpreter
and the compiled code call; that the interpreter loads a helper beside its glue
classes, taking among the methods of that name the one whose Java parameter and
result types carry the declared types, \KWD{self} first, and carrying each value
at its declared type; that the compiler, before type checking, rewrites such a
body into a call of the helper, which the type checker checks against the
helper's Java signature; and that a string under that package that names no
such method is an error on both.
It also names the package that defines the subclasses of the classes
\texttt{NativeFn0} to \texttt{NativeFn4}
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim}, where it said
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.primitive}, a package that the
implementation does not have.
The comment gains a box.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 10~October 2026 that every native binding of \library\
keeps the library's own form, a body that is exactly a call of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive}, and that its string names a static helper of the
package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, the compiled code's own
helpers, in place of a glue class, which takes the interpreter's values and
which the compiled code cannot call.
The bindings move onto helpers step by step, and the type checker checks each
- A string that names a glue class, or a declaration with a varargs parameter, does not stop the check. The body stays a call of `builtinPrimitive`, typed at the declared result type, and no Java signature checks it (ledger row 849).
- The checker reads a helper's Java types as the interpreter's library's types: `String` as `String`, not `JavaString`, and the rest as in a compile.
- A component that imports a DSL grammar is parsed by other code (`GraphRepository.syntaxExpand`), which does not rewrite its bindings. So, as for a glue class, no Java signature checks them.
- The count stage checks only the `FortressLibrary` component's bindings. A binding of another component, as `FortressBuiltin`'s, only the distance stage checks.

The checker, in a compile and in both stages, reads `int` as `NN32` or `Char`, and `long` as `NN64`, only for six helpers with fixed names (`NamingCzar.java:373-384`, `:494-503`). Examples are `makeNN32FromZZ32WithSpecialCompilerHackForNN32ResultType` for a result and `makeZZ32FromNN32WithSpecialCompilerHackForNN32ArgumentType` for a parameter. So a binding over `NN32`, `NN64` or `Char` that names any other helper is a type error for the checker. Walk loads it, because it carries these types in `int` and `long`.

The wrapper generator wraps every method of a class that it is given, the private methods too. If a type has no Fortress counterpart, it fails the whole import. So give every method of a helper class a signature that maps to Fortress, also a private method.

content.content:
\subsection{Prefix Operators}
\seclabel{prefixops}

For all standard numeric types, the prefix operator \EXP{+} simply returns its
argument and the prefix operator \EXP{-} returns the negative of its argument.

The operator \EXP{\neg} is the logical \scap{not} operator on boolean values
and boolean intervals.

The operator \EXP{\twointersectnot} computes the bitwise \scap{not} of
an integer.

Big operators such as \EXP{\sum} begin a \emph{reduction expression}
(\secref{reduction-expr}).  The big operators include \EXP{\sum}
(summation) and \EXP{\prod} (product), along with \EXP{\bigcap},
\EXP{\bigcup}, \EXP{\bigwedge}, \EXP{\bigvee},
\EXP{\underline{\bigvee}}, \EXP{\bigoplus},
\EXP{\bigotimes}, \EXP{\biguplus}, \EXP{\displaystyle\boxplus},
\EXP{\displaystyle\boxtimes}, \OPR{MAX}, \OPR{MIN}, and so on.

\subsection{Multiplication, Division, Modulo, and Remainder Operators}

For most integer, rational, floating-point, complex, and interval expressions,
multiplication can be expressed using any of `\EXP{\cdot}' or
`\EXP{\times}' or simply juxtaposition.
However,
the \EXP{\times} operator is used to
express the shape of matrices, so if expressions using multiplication are used
in expressing the shape of a matrix, it may be necessary to avoid the
use of '\EXP{\times}' to
express multiplication, or to use parentheses.

For integer, rational, floating-point, complex, and interval expressions, division is expressed by \EXP{/}.
When the operator \EXP{/} is used to divide one integer by another,
the result is rational.
The operator \EXP{\div} performs truncating integer division:
\EXP{m \div n = \mathit{signum}\left({m \over n}\right) \left\lfloor \left| {m \over n} \right| \right\rfloor}.
The operator \OPR{REM} gives the remainder from such a truncating division:
\EXP{m \OPR{REM} n = m - n (m \div n)}.
The operator \OPR{MOD} gives the remainder from a floor division:
\EXP{m \OPR{MOD} n = m - n \left\lfloor {m \over n} \right\rfloor};
when \EXP{n>0} this is the usual modulus computation that evaluates integer \VAR{m}
to an integer \VAR{k} such that \EXP{0\leq{}k<n} and \VAR{n} evenly divides \EXP{m-k}.

\marginnote{This is not true: Character literals include ``\b'' and
``LATIN CAPITAL A'', which do not ``consist of'' an abstract character enclosed in
single quotation marks.  I think it's better to remove most of this discussion and
direct the reader to the relevant section of Lexical Structure.
This section should be about {\bf semantics} of literals:
their values and types.}
For convenience,
the marks may be true typographical ``curly'' single quotation marks
(U+2018 and U+2019),
a pair of apostrophe characters (U+0027),
or a ``backquote'' character (U+0060) and an apostrophe character.
It is a static error if the opening and closing marks do not match:
a character literal beginning with a left single quotation mark
must end with a right single quotation mark;
one beginning with either an apostrophe or a backquote
must end with an apostrophe.
As discussed in \secref{literals},
a character literal evaluates to a value of type \TYP{Char},
which represents an abstract Unicode character.

A left single quotation mark (U+2018) or a backquote
begins a character literal
unless it is within a comment, another character literal,
or a string literal.

### Forks the batch takes, none consequential

Each default can be undone, and none reverses a decision of his or touches a line of microGPT.

1. **Seven rungs, F, Z, S, K, W, G and H, the manifest's order; none lands only with another; the gather applies them by its rule, F, K, Z, S, W, G, H.** Default: so. No rung builds on another: each one's tests pass on its own tree. F, Z and S share two library files, at different declarations; F and W share `StaticNativeApp.java`, at different declarations (fork 4); K shares `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` with Z and S, at the two `CHOOSE` declarations. The gather's rule puts two rungs that share a file in the ascending order of their lowest edited line in it, and keeps the manifest's order for rungs that share none (`climb-batch-workflow.md`, "Gather"): K's first string, `FortressLibrary.fss:789`, is above Z's, `:832`, and S's, `:986`, so K goes before Z and S; F goes before S (`FortressBuiltin.fss:56` against `:380`) and before W (`StaticNativeApp.java:51` against `:81`). No line moves 
2. **K takes `CHOOSE` on both `ZZ32` and `ZZ64`, as a rung of its own.** Default: the CHOOSE probe recommends `CHOOSE` in this batch with the helper's fix in the rung that moves the binding, the record deciding the fix (`plan-24/probes/choose.md`, sections 1 and 8: the specification's coefficient and its `IntegerOverflow`, P-73, row 521's fix); its patch fixes `simpleIntArith` only. K takes that patch and makes the same two fixes in `simpleLongArith`, whose same two faults the probe measured, and moves both `CHOOSE` bindings. The ways not taken: `ZZ32`'s alone, which leaves `XXXChooseTableCompiledRungE` an expected failure, since it asserts both helpers, and leaves `ZZ64`'s `CHOOSE` and row 855's `ZZ64` half to a later batch with no rung named; or the `ZZ64` half inside Z, which would put an edit of helpers that both paths run, and both paths' suites, into a rung of library text. A rung 
3. **F carries walk's carry of `Float`, one line of `StaticNativeApp.javaFor`.** Default: so. Walk's loader carries a declared parameter type only by name, and `Float` is not among its names (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:47-58`), so the planner's sample move of `Float`'s `+` alone stopped every program at load: 'Native helper com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleDoubleArith.doubleAdd: no Java type carries the declared type of parameter b.' Twelve of the 30 have a parameter declared `Float`. The ways not taken: the declarations rewritten at `RR64`, which changes `Float`'s headers and its overloads; the carry put in W, on which F's tests would then build.
4. **W's check of `self`: the closure tells the loader the type that declares the method, and the loader takes that type's Java carrier from its own table.** Default: `MethodClosure` passes its `definer` and `FunctionalMethod` its self type through `NativeApp.checkAndLoadNative` to `StaticNativeApp.find`, which refuses at load a method whose declaring type no Java type carries, 'Native helper ...: no Java type carries Holder, the type of self.', and takes only an overload whose first Java parameter is that carrier; a top-level function is told no type and is loaded as today. The table, `javaForSelf`, is `javaFor`'s names plus the value objects `Int`, `Long`, `UnsignedLong`, `Float` and `BigNum`, so W carries `Float` for `self` without F's line, and the two rungs change different declarations. The ways not taken: a refusal at the call, where row 847 asks for one at load; the declaring typ

The compiled guard cannot declare a method on the pr

Row 848's half is H's, since H moves `NN32`'s and `NN64`'s `DIV` onto helpers that raise: H writes `NN32DivisionByZeroWalk` and `NN64DivisionByZeroWalk`, failing on the base 
7. **The Appendix I entry's Effect is the gather's.** Default: no rung edits `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`. Its entry "A native binding that names a static helper" states the count of moved bindings, `CHOOSE`'s state, the divisions by zero that end the run, and row 847 (`changes.tex:4466-4502`), so F, Z, S, K, W and H each make a sentence of it false; one declaration changed by six rungs breaks the batch's rule. Row 307 gains a note.
14. **No speed pass.** No rung changes the checker's code: G changes the code generator, which the stages do not run.
15. **No rung declares a checker count, a crash or a ladder move.** All 85 ladder programs pass at climb batch 23's gate, so none can move.
16. **Rows.** Default: W closes 847; K closes 521 and 855; Z rewrites 336 and sets its reproducer; S sets the reproducers of 856 and 857; H rewrites 848 and sets its reproducer and 860's; G rewrites 701 and notes 307. Rows filed by plan, before the launch, at the coordinator's word: 855, the race of the two `CHOOSE` helpers (the CHOOSE probe's draft), 856 (`signed` above the signed range), 857 (`char` out of range), 860 (the `NN64` wrapping negation's helper answers its operand) and 861 (`Char`'s `asExprString` in two forms). Any other defect a rung meets gets its row through its `record.md`, as the manual gives it.

With the 80 moved for one run, 91 of 1,325 printed values changed, every one from those four; with them back, none. The ways not taken: H fixes the two `NN64` helpers (`Long.toUnsignedString`, `-a`), which would change the prelude's compiled `NN64` printing and `BOXMINUS` too and bring nativeHelpers into a rung of the rewrite; or moves them with the change of va

- **Team lines changed:** H, 76 strings of `value object NN32`, `trait NN64` and `value object Char`, and the revival's `BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter`; F, 30 strings of `value object Float` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:54-194`); Z, 36 strings of `trait ZZ64` and `trait ZZ` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:818-909`, `:991-1085`); S, 8 strings in both files; K, the two `CHOOSE` strings and one line in each of `simpleIntArith.intOverflowingChoose` and `simpleLongArith.longOverflowingChoose`; W, the team's `FunctionClosure`, `MethodClosure`, `FunctionalMethod` and `NativeApp.checkAndLoadNative`; G, three lines of the team's `CodeGen`. `StaticNativeApp` is the revival's.

**Verdict: approved.** The change is the planner's `rung-H.patch`, its Java differing only in two comments and one equivalent expression, and its 76 strings equal to the patch line for line. The branch already held both files, at `967e595ca`. So the brief's two `journal-text.py` lines wrote nothing (`[ -e … ] ||`). I wrote the journal's texts to scratch, and `diff` against the committed `REPORT.md` and `record.md` printed nothing, so the branch carries the journal's texts byte for byte.

1. **The tables.** The worker's count table, `diff`ed against `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-23/gate/checker-count.txt`, prints nothing. Call `1M3Wcj` at 11:30:14 gives 'NN32 DIV by zero: DivisionByZero', 'NN64 DIV by zero: DivisionByZero' and 'OK (14 tests)'.

data.summary:
Rung H is right, and I approve it. The Java is the planner's rung-H.patch with only two comments reworded and one equivalent expression (BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:23-31, :126, :132-134). I applied the patch to the base's files in scratch and diffed them against the head: the 76 library strings are identical. The tests came first, through the harness, on the base's code:
- walk at 11:21 (call BdrMx3, 'Tests run: 6,  Failures: 2', the two division tests with 'Caused by: java.lang.ArithmeticException: / by zero');
- compiled at 11:25 (call BMgz7Z, 'File NativeHelperTransferCompiled.fss has 71 errors.');
- the patch was applied at 11:26:46 and built at 11:27:34;
- after the build: 'OK (16 tests)' and 'OK (14 tests)'.

The count and distance tables match the worker's files and climb batch 23's gate tables, apart from the time and machine rows. The tables are those of the worker's head; I ran no stage, since the diff changes no checker Scala.

My own programs, old code against new:
- SkHWalk1, 2,571 printed values under walk at FORTRESS_THREADS 1 and 4: the 39 Char bindings at out-of-range and edge code points, comparisons the library derives from the moved `<`, strToInt, NN32 and NN64 through derived and generic library code, and parallel reductions. `diff` prints nothing.
- SkHWalk2: a helper's IntegerOverflow, caught and uncaught, looks the same as the glue class's.
- SkHComp1: binding shapes the worker did not test (mixed NN32 and ZZ32 or ZZ64 positions, an NN64 position with ZZ32, an RR64 result, a transfer around a transfer, a function value). The old code refuses it with 9 errors; the new code gives PASS at 1 and 4 threads.
- SkHComp3: three misfitting bindings stay refused on both codes.

Failure mode: the transfers are identities, so a binding over NN32 of a signed helper (simpleIntArith.intLT) now compiles and answers true for 2^31 < 1. The old checker refused it, and walk already answers so on both codes.

I made two record corrections, commit 4af5d05bc:
- The FACTS hand-over said a binding in a generic owner gets no transfer. Only `self` goes without one there; it now says so, with the failure-mode sentence added.
- F-24 is added to the entries the rung makes stale.

SKEPTIC.md is committed last, as 696a79095, and pushed. No fix of mine is contested, and no code changed.
